newsitem.title: USA: Norland resolves issues raised by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Norland resolves issues raised by FDA.

text.p: Norland Medical Systems Inc on Tuesday said that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has resolved issues raised with its Norland Corp unit in June.

The FDA had sent Norland a warning letter which claimed that the pDEXA bone densitometer made by Norland Corp did not comply with certain regulations regarding field size limitation and the labeling of certain x-ray components.

Norland said that the FDA rescinded its claim of non-compliance with field size limitation regulations and acknowledged that the claim was based on a misunderstanding resulting from inaccurate information inadvertently supplied to the agency by Norland.

Norland said it has agreed to include date and place of manufacture information on the labels for the parts in question. FDA agreed with Norland that the failure to provide such information did not create a significant risk of injury to the user and granted an exemption from such labeling requirements for all pDEXA units previously sold, it said.

"I am pleased to confirm that the warning letter issues have been resolved and that there will be no recall of the pDEXA," said Reynald Bonmati, chairman and president of Norland Medical Systems, in a written statement.
